feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the content signals both strategic and hands-on capability. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive and dense, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within one organization strongly support leadership growth and trust.  
- Good impact signals: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms add substance.  
- Strong positioning: combines strategy, operations, content, analytics, and technical execution in a way that fits senior digital roles well.

1. Top improvements  
- Tighten repetition and structure: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to reduce redundancy and improve scanability.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results; include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, or campaign performance.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: use “12 years of experience” (not “12 years experience”); standardize serial comma usage (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); consider “full-time freelance engagement” instead of “Freelance (full-time engagement)” for smoother phrasing.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be stronger with sharper positioning, a more concise structure, and one or two specifics that reflect recent enterprise-scale work.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten phrasing and fix style: use “12+ years of experience” instead of “more than 12 years experience.”
- Lead with current senior value proposition: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Add a concrete scale or context from recent roles (for example, enterprise web platforms, large publisher groups, or advocacy/member organizations).
- Reduce generic wording like “strong background” and replace with more direct, outcome-oriented language.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven and advocacy-focused organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, platform modernization, and the systems, governance, and workflows that support complex teams. Experienced in stakeholder coordination and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant mix of strategic, technical, and operational strengths, but several items are broad or overlap heavily with the header and Topline Skills. Tightening wording and emphasizing higher-value leadership themes will make this section sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic phrases with more senior, specific language: “Multi-channel communications leadership,” “CMS governance & administration,” and “Analytics, insights & performance reporting.”
- Reduce repetition by combining similar items: merge “Editorial workflow design” with “Workflow & systems architecture” into “Editorial operations, workflow & systems design.”
- Prioritize most marketable strengths first: Digital strategy & transformation • Enterprise web/CMS leadership • Editorial operations • Analytics • Stakeholder coordination.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications leadership • Enterprise web & CMS governance • Editorial operations, workflow & systems design • Analytics, insights & performance reporting • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” repeats the header and Soft Skills section.
- “Web & CMS administration” and analytics language overlap with Topline Skills and Technical + IT.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps with the “Recent Projects” footer and prior NACo entries. Tighten it around scope, systems leadership, and 2–3 concrete outcomes or flagship builds.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + client type + remit: “Embedded as a full-time freelance consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, web operations, and campaign platform development.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets into impact-led statements: “Built Drupal-based campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and member toolkits; improved publishing flexibility and campaign launch speed.”
- Combine systems/governance/analytics into one bullet with outcomes: “Streamlined cross-channel workflows, governance, and analytics across web, email, social, and multimedia to improve coordination and reporting.” Add metrics if possible.
- Make the AI/search work outcome-based: “Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content, and discovery UX to improve findability of complex policy/member content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current microsite/AI-search wording duplicates the “Recent Projects” section; keep this entry higher-level and leave project specifics there.
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats prior NACo role language; emphasize what is new or more advanced here.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if the opening is tighter, bullets start with outcomes, and channel-management points avoid repeating older NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget across enterprise communications.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel bullet more outcome-based: add growth, engagement, send volume, or campaign performance if available; otherwise shorten to avoid generic scope language.
- Tighten the rest: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio…” / “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting…” / “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this item focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video/programming language also appears in earlier NACo roles; emphasize building the studio and scaling in-house capacity here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what you owned at this level: executional leadership, editorial cadence, and channel-building.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add clearer outcome language where possible: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger line: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is very similar to the Director role; reduce channel-list repetition.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role, so frame this here as scaling/formalizing the series, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize differentiators and language that reflects recent senior-level scope.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, senior-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy for mission-driven organizations
- Editorial governance and scalable content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Keep wording parallel: use either all noun phrases or all “X and Y” constructions.
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” or “strategy” to sound more executive and less tactical.
- If space allows, add one qualifier tied to scale, e.g. “enterprise” or “organization-wide,” rather than trying to force metrics into a skills list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Core Competencies” (“Digital governance & editorial systems,” “Multi-channel communications operations,” “Advocacy and public-sector communications”).
- “Audience-focused content planning” overlaps with work-history language on editorial planning; keep only if phrased more strategically.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills item, make it more strategic, grouped, and aligned to recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped capabilities, e.g.: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages • CMS modernization & front-end implementation • HTML, CSS, JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Lead with Drupal and CMS modernization since recent roles emphasize Drupal platform rebuilds, microsites, and enterprise web improvement.
- Replace “technical execution” jargon with clearer value language like “front-end implementation” or “platform delivery.”
- If space allows, sharpen with scope: “Enterprise CMS modernization” or “AI-enabled search for complex content discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave tool-by-tool detail to that section.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrasing across both sections.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tools-only to outcomes-led language, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Decision-support reporting” for clearer business value.
- Tighten and group related items: tools first, then strategic capabilities; avoid eight separate fragments.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one measurable proof point tied to recent work, such as supporting reporting for a 10,000+ page site or 3.5M annual page views.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This is highly redundant with “Technical + IT → Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep this section strategic and let the technical section hold the full tool list.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may partially overlap with broader “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it’s too generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and operational scope rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task list to leadership/production capability: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to better match the NACo studio build and seniority.
- Drop “editing” unless it’s a differentiator you want surfaced here; tools already appear under Technical + IT.
- If space allows, use “Studio build-out and operations” instead of just “Studio operations” to reflect stronger impact from the 2022–2024 role.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Multimedia production and livestream operations”; vary wording or remove one.
- PTZ/studio details may be better left here, while general multimedia capability stays in Core Competencies.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or reframed to show level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize the most relevant/recent tools first: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add proficiency context rather than just names: “Enterprise CMS administration: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages; lightweight publishing: GitHub Pages.”
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; use either “CMS” or “Web Platforms & CMS Administration” to better match the leadership/operations angle.
- If GitHub Pages was only occasional use, consider dropping it to keep the list sharper and more senior.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid repeating it elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools actually used in recent roles and group items more clearly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Front-end & implementation:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery; **Integrations & deployment:** API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers unless they matter; use **HTML/CSS/JavaScript** for cleaner phrasing.
- Consider replacing broad tools with stronger proof of application if accurate, e.g. **custom Drupal front-end implementation**, **tag deployment**, **serverless scripting**, or **CI/CD support**.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect one item to impact in experience bullets rather than here, since skills sections are strongest when concise.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Technical Implementation” partially overlaps with recent work bullets on CMS development/front-end implementation; avoid repeating the same phrasing.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” and Airtable systems already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more clearly framed around orchestration/operations tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation, PM & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strongest/relevant tools first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- Drop weaker/dated items unless actively used recently: remove **Basecamp** if it’s not important to current/frequent work.
- If space allows, add light grouping for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; keep them only if they support a broader systems/operations narrative.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent roles, this line should emphasize platform depth and engagement systems rather than repeat “email” generally.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and standardize platform names: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers to show level of use: **campaign operations, newsletter publishing, audience segmentation, and engagement workflows**
- Example rewrite: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (campaign deployment, newsletter operations, segmentation, engagement workflows)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding broad claims like “email strategy” or “newsletter leadership” here; those are already covered in recent NACo roles.
- If Higher Logic was the primary platform in your most recent relevant work, consider listing it first to better reflect recency.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this reads broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs and team-building impact.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as early-stage team building: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team and establish workflows across web, email, social and video.”
- Add specific scope/results where possible: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or process improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce stacked clauses: split team-building, website work, content production, and supervision into distinct achievements.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, formalizing workflows across web, email, social and video. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates. Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate and helped expand in-house multimedia capacity.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations language; keep this version more tactical.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media production. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the policy/research support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Supported county innovation and policy initiatives through research, program coordination, and digital content development.”
- Add a stronger second sentence: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with specific outputs if possible: web articles, interviews, audio segments, campaign assets, etc.
- If available, add scale or outcome: number of episodes launched, audience growth, internal adoption, or how the podcast supported member engagement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media roles; keep this item focused on research/program support plus the first podcast launch.
- Avoid overstating leadership in digital operations here, since stronger leadership evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.
